title: Unraveling Block Maxima Forecasting Models with Counterfactual Explanation

problem.claim: Block maxima forecasting can support applications where extreme values signify critical events, while increasing use of deep neural networks creates a need to explain their forecasts.

gap.claim: Existing explainability methods do not provide the proposed counterfactual explanation approach for block maxima forecasting models.

contributions.claim: The paper presents DiffusionCF, a counterfactual explanation framework for block maxima forecasting models.
DiffusionCF combines deep anomaly detection with a conditional diffusion model to identify unusual time-series patterns that may explain forecasted extreme block maxima.
The authors provide data and code for DiffusionCF.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their counterfactual explanation framework for block maxima forecasting models as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on several real-world datasets report that DiffusionCF outperforms baseline methods on various metrics, particularly informativeness and closeness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Extreme block maxima forecasts can matter for disease surveillance, traffic management, and weather forecasting.
The growth of deep neural network use increases the need for explainability in block maxima forecasting.
The paper introduces a counterfactual explanation framework called DiffusionCF.
DiffusionCF combines deep anomaly detection and conditional diffusion to identify unusual explanatory time-series patterns.
Real-world dataset experiments report superiority over baselines on several metrics.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines anomaly detection with conditional diffusion to generate counterfactual explanations for extreme forecasts.

interpretation.claim: Explanations for extreme-value forecasts may benefit from modeling unusual temporal patterns rather than only attributing feature importance.

application.claim: For other critical-event forecasting systems, consider counterfactual explanations that identify plausible unusual patterns associated with the forecast.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond block maxima forecasting or all listed application domains.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metric values, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the counterfactual generation procedure or model architecture in detail.
The abstract does not report limitations, computational costs, or reproducibility details beyond the availability of data and code.
